> `modversion` does not provide driver version 

You could try to fetch the Mesa version somehow if on an open source driver. Knowing the kernel + Mesa version is generally a reliable way to figure out the actual "driver version" of open source drivers.

Thank you for the pointers.

I skimmed over the arch docs (https://wiki.archlinux.org/title/Intel_graphics), but couldn't find anything regarding Intel driver version.  
Then I found this https://askubuntu.com/a/1163453 comment, which makes sense: there is no real driver version for Intel graphics cards.

checking the outputs for my i915 driver:
```sh
$ glxinfo -B | grep "OpenGL ES profile version string"
OpenGL ES profile version string: OpenGL ES 3.2 Mesa 25.0.7-0ubuntu0.24.04.2

$ uname -r
6.14.0-35-generic
```

Based on all the new info, I'd continue like this
* if `modprobe` returns no version, then combine the result of the two commands above (+ some cleanup), e.g. `6.14.0-35-generic | OpenGL ES 3.2 Mesa 25.0.7-0ubuntu0.24.04.2`
* make a second attempt at cleanup: use `OS.get_distribution_name()` to split the string and take the string before the split. result: `6.14.0-35-generic | OpenGL ES 3.2 Mesa 25.0.7-0`
* _edit_: with more elaborate use of `glxinfo` (see updated PR description), we can shorten it to
  * name: `i915` and version: `6.14.0-35-generic | Mesa 25.0.7`
  * **compatibility renderer** will require an improved version of the previous elaborate guesswork (if multiple graphics cards)

What do you think?

This func returns a different level of drivers, the [kernel drivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Direct_Rendering_Manager#Hardware_support): i915, amdgpu, radeon, nvidia, etc.

Looking at your output, the following two commands should deliver the kernel driver (probably `radeonsi`) for your GPUs (see line `Kernel driver in use:`)
```sh
lspci -d 4098:6400 -k
lspci -d 4098:29824 -k
```

and modinfo should deliver the version
```sh
# or `radeon`, or `amdgpu`
modinfo -p radeonsi | grep "version:"
```

But amdgpu is part of the Linux kernel AFAIK, so its version is the kernel version.

What matters for Mesa drivers on Linux is:
- Kernel version
- Mesa version
- DRM version
- LLVM version used by Mesa drivers

Which is all information that Godot already gathered for its startup info message, at least for OpenGL:
```
OpenGL API 4.6 (Core Profile) Mesa 25.2.6 - Compatibility - Using Device: AMD - AMD Radeon 780M Graphics (radeonsi, phoenix, LLVM 21.1.4, DRM 3.64, 6.17.7-300.fc43.x86_64)
...
OpenGL API 4.6 (Core Profile) Mesa 25.2.6 - Compatibility - Using Device: AMD - AMD Radeon RX 7600M XT (radeonsi, navi33, LLVM 21.1.4, DRM 3.64, 6.17.7-300.fc43.x86_64)
...
Vulkan 1.4.318 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: AMD - AMD Radeon 780M Graphics (RADV PHOENIX)
...
Vulkan 1.4.318 - Forward+ - Using Device #0: AMD - AMD Radeon RX 7600M XT (RADV NAVI33)
```

> Those device IDs don't work for me

yikes, sorry. Wrong format

---

Okaay, so Godot prints for OpenGL basically the content of `glxinfo -B` and the lines with `OpenGL core profile version string:` and `Device:`.  
For my Intel-based device, I get no info on DRM and LLVM version. Only "Mesa" and its version "25.0.7"

To summarize: In your case (using glxfinfo), you get additionally
* `radeonsi`, which is the Mesa driver name in _user-space_. But afaik that info is not useful, because it just says "I'm responsible for OpenGL". `radv` is for Vulkan. I'd say out-of-scope.
* "navi33" and "phoenix". these are just GPU names. out-of-scope.
* the Linux kernel version, but there's already `uname -r`
*  DRM and LLVM versions

Based on that, I'd change the output to
```
# your case
amdgpu
Linux 6.17.7-300 | Mesa 25.2.6 (LLVM 21.1.4, DRM 3.64)

# my case
i915
Linux 6.14.0-35-generic | Mesa 25.0.7
```

process:
* using OS.get_name() for "Linux", just in case it's *BSD
* simple string-contains-check for "Mesa" in line `OpenGL core profile version string:` of glxinfo output. If not found for some reason, write whole line and prefix "OpenGL API" (to fit the output Godot already gives)
* get Mesa version by reading line `Version:` of glxinfo output
* lookup "LLVM" and "DRM" in line `OpenGL renderer string` of glxinfo output
Sounds good to me. We probably want to cache the result of all these system calls and string concatenation so that we don't re-do it all the time if a user runs it in `_process` for some reason.

> We probably want to cache the result

Most definitely!  
This was added the first time around, so it's already cached thanks to `static Vector<String> info;`

> If there's a way to retrieve the GPU devices count reported in that warning (not emitted by Godot)

You can trigger that warning like so:
```sh
DRI_PRIME=99 eglinfo -B

# then go to X11 or Wayland platform block:
Wayland platform:
Inconsistent value (99) for DRI_PRIME. Should be < 1 (GPU devices count). Using: 0

# or use
DRI_PRIME=99 glxlinfo -B
# warning is in the line after display name
name of display: :0
Inconsistent value (99) for DRI_PRIME. Should be < 1 (GPU devices count). Using: 0
```

Or use  
`eglinfo -B`  
and get the highest number in `Device #{number}:` (while it starts counting at 0, the last one is always Mesa itself. Therefore the highest number is also the device count).
